references.text: The cloud covered the tabernacle when it was erected, and the glory of the Lord filled the dwelling. This is the original account of the cloud that covered the tabernacle.
Describes how the Lord's cloud was over the tabernacle by day, and fire was over it by night, visible to all the house of Israel.
The Lord went before the people in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night. This is the first mention of the cloud and fire that led Israel.
The tent of testimony (אֹהֶל הָעֵדֻת) is mentioned here in connection with the ark of the covenant and God's presence.
Continuation of the description of the cloud covering the tabernacle and the appearance of fire by night.
Moses reminds the people how the Lord went before them in fire by night and cloud by day.
When Solomon's temple was dedicated, the cloud filled the house, just as with the tabernacle. God's glory manifested itself in the same way.
Parallel to the temple dedication where the cloud filled the Lord's house, reflecting the tabernacle.
Isaiah prophesies that the Lord will create a cloud by day and smoke and shining fire by night over Mount Zion.
Ezekiel sees the glory of the Lord rise up and the cloud fill the house, recalling the tabernacle.
